name: Subsea Christmas Tree Standard Benchmark
description: As offshore oil and gas development progresses toward high-pressure, high-temperature, and increasingly complex working conditions, the improvement of standard systems for subsea Christmas trees and wellhead equipment becomes critical to ensuring production safety and efficiency. This study, for the first time, constructs a multi-dimensional benchmarking evaluation system, systematically comparing the GB/T 22513 standard with the internationally advanced ISO 10423 standard across five dimensions: material selection, manufacturing processes, testing methods, quality control, and environmental adaptability. By innovatively integrating the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and the Entropy Weight Method to quantify weights, and employing the Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation method to assess the technical level and applicability, the study reveals that ISO 10423 demonstrates significant advantages in terms of technical coverage and environmental adaptability, making it more suitable for high-end operating conditions. In contrast, GB/T 22513 shows strengths in economic efficiency and implementation feasibility, making it more appropriate for medium-pressure and normal-temperature environments. This research provides a scientific basis for optimizing GB/T 22513 and aligning it with international standards, thereby promoting the high-quality and globalized development of oil and gas equipment standards.
evaluation_method: composite score using AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process) + Entropy Weight + Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation
general_score_metric: composite weighted score from AHP/entropy-weighted fuzzy evaluation
reputation: Academic/industry-focused study used for standards comparison in offshore oil & gas; limited adoption outside standards and engineering communities.
notes: Not a machine-learning benchmark. Results are methodology-sensitive and involve subjective weighting; applicability limited to standards analysis and engineering decision-making.
